method: After freezing the decision and record, returned to Articles 3.3 and 3.5 and Appendices 1–3, the official course planner entry and the thesis and profiling pages. Rebuilt the credit groups and level totals independently and checked the course-year progression. Reviewed the current UCR workbook for offerings and substantive contributions, then checked the finished pair and reader-facing content against those findings in a separate same-AI pass.
findings: The 2026–27 full-time Utrecht Art History bachelor is taught principally in Dutch. The regulations set a 120 EC major and 60 EC of profiling. The major comprises eight 7.5 EC introductory courses, two 7.5 EC context courses, four 7.5 EC courses in one formal depth package and an advanced 15 EC individual thesis. The first-listed Art and Architecture before 1850 package is selected independently of UCR fit. Its four 7.5 EC courses, the 7.5 EC heritage context course and 15 EC thesis supply 52.5 advanced EC, exceeding the 45 EC major minimum. The 60 EC profiling contains a coherent 30 EC package and must include at least 15 EC at level 2 or 3. Its individual selections remain open.

The first-year foundational packages are compulsory. The older-art depth package follows one course per block, including the excursion in Block 3 and research seminar in Block 4. The official planner requires 15 EC at level 3 before the individual 15 EC final paper and lists the relevant research seminar as prior knowledge. Completing the Year 2 depth package gives 30 EC at level 3 and the seminar before Year 3. The thesis runs over Blocks 1–2 or 3–4. The two mandatory context courses are listed in Blocks 2 and 3; remaining profiling can be chosen around those commitments. The thesis is supervised and individually written. The example illustrates the 2026–27 structure with non-overlapping elective choices subject to availability.

The three plans make different use of art, objects, historical sources, museums and modern media. The closest and modern options retain their courses. The earlier-art option adds literary interpretation and historical philosophy while preserving direct older-art coursework. The comparison retains the architecture and excursion gaps and the different research requirements.
